The terms that do not involve index $k$ are identical in both sums and cancel out. The terms involving index $k$ depend on whether $k$ is at the boundaries ($1$ or $n$) or in the interior ($1 < k < n$).

    Since $x_{k-1} = x'_{k-1}$ and $x_{k+1} = x'_{k+1}$:
    $$ \text{Difference} = (x_{k-1} + x_{k+1})(x_k - x'_k) $$
    Taking the absolute value:
    $$ |f(X) - f(X')| = |x_{k-1} + x_{k+1}| \cdot |x_k - x'_k| $$
    Since $x_i \in [0, 1]$, the maximum value of $(x_{k-1} + x_{k+1})$ is $1 + 1 = 2$. The maximum value of $|x_k - x'_k|$ is $1 - 0 = 1$.

The global sensitivity is the maximum of these cases, so $\Delta f = 2$.
